name: Exclusion
oneLine: Shutting one or two ego states out of use almost entirely - excluding Parent, Adult or Child, or running constantly on just one of the three - as a fixed strategy, not a passing mood.
whatYouDid: You asked whether Victor's unbroken, question-free certainty was a counterfeit version of "constant Adult" - someone who never doubts and never asks - and why that's worse than it sounds once you know the Adult underneath is contaminated.
confusion: People confuse exclusion with simply preferring one ego state; the tell is that exclusion means the other states are close to unavailable, not just less used - someone with an excluded Child genuinely can't recall childhood feelings on request, not merely that they don't lead with feelings day to day.

fromBook.quote: Eric Berne named these two problems contamination and exclusion.

expand.definition: Excluding one ego state entirely (no Parent, no Adult, or no Child) or running as "constant/excluding" in just one (constant Parent, constant Adult, or constant Child) means that state is barely reachable in that person, not just rarely chosen; Berne noted exclusion is never total, only extreme in particular situations.
expand.otherFraming: TA Today warns that someone who looks like "constant Adult" - all data, no fun, "unable to join in" - can be mistaken for the healthiest person in the room, when really a third of their personality has gone dark.
expand.tryThisToday: Ask yourself honestly: is there one of Parent, Adult or Child you can almost never access, even when you try? That's worth noticing, independent of which one you simply use most.
